transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-11-16
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (CSM), Jordan (Rivermark Eng Mgr), Maya (Rivermark Platform), Samir (Rivermark ML), Tina (Rivermark Security)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on latency tuning. Reviewed latest TTFT numbers, streaming behavior, sequence length impact, and kernel selection. Agreed next tests and ownerships; will share benchmark sheet and schedule a canary once perf improvements validated.

Topics: TTFT (time to first token), streaming vs immediate batch, sequence length distributions, kernel/quantization choices, VPC profiling for Private deployment, security concerns (audit/logging).

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: ok hi everyone thanks for carving out time, uh this is our weekly latency tuning sync for the Rivermark POC. uh quick roll call, alex from redwood, priya, liam.
[00:08] Jordan: hey alex yeah jordan here, maya and samir are on as well, tina will be on for the security bits.
[00:14] Priya: hey, super. quick agenda — share the latest numbers we ran yesterday, talk TTFT, streaming, sequence length, kernel choices and then line up next steps. sound ok?
[00:22] Jordan: yep that works.
[00:25] Priya: cool. so quick context — we re-ran the workload with the model pinned to r-infer-v2 (our internal shorthand), on dedicated gpus with quant 4-bit. previous run had TTFT ~210ms for 32-token prompts, today we see TTFT down to 165ms after switching kernel set to fast-attn-asm and enabling early kv warmup.
[00:45] Samir: nice where are we measuring TTFT though, is that at the ingress point or after tokenization?
[00:50] Priya: good q — that's measured from request arrival at the runtime to first token emitted, includes tokenization. we can break it down in the sheet; the biggest wins were kernel swap + prefetching the KV cache when we detect prefix reuse.
[01:05] Maya: when you say prefetching KV, do you mean Redwood's prefix cache or something we need to configure in our VPC?
[01:12] Priya: it's an option in the runtime — automatic prefix/KV caching. it works transparently but for private deployment you can tune the cache size and eviction policy. for rivermark we bumped the cache from default 2GB to 6GB which cut a bunch of lookups.
[01:25] Jordan: ok that explains some of the drop. can you also share the kernel config? we saw some instability when we tried a different kernel set earlier.
[01:33] Alex: yeah i'll share the kernel config and the benchmark spreadsheet right after the call — link will be in the follow-up. (note: the link points to the benchmark doc)
[01:40] Tina: security question, does caching store customer data in plaintext on the node fs? we need to know retention and encryption behaviour.
[01:48] Priya: good catch — KV cache is encrypted at rest using the node KMS by default in Dedicated; in Private we can plug your KMS, yes the cache is ephemeral per pod and TTL is configurable.
[01:58] Tina: ok please add that to the security doc you share.
[02:03] Priya: will do. next — streaming. we turned streaming on for the same test and saw TTFT improve but end-to-end 95th pct tail didn't move as much because the tail is dominated by long sequences.
[02:17] Samir: when you say streaming improved TTFT, are you seeing partial tokens earlier or is it the same first token earlier?
[02:22] Priya: partial tokens — we emit partial hypotheses earlier with streaming which lowers perceived TTFT. but if downstream does blockage waiting for full answer, benefits shrink.
[02:33] Jordan: our UI consumes streaming progressively so this helps, but our main concern is 95th pct under load; long sequences (500+ tokens) push pods into memory pressure and kernel fallback which spikes latency.
[02:46] Priya: yep long seqs are the main driver. we tested sequence buckets 64/128/256/512; on 512 we saw kernel fallback to safe_attention which is slower. on 64/128 streaming + batch packing gave us best throughput and lowest TTFT.
[03:02] Maya: can we prioritize reducing the 95th pct for 256/512 sequences? that's our main SLA.
[03:08] Priya: plan — run targeted profiling for the 256/512 bucket with alternate kernel sets: fast-attn-asm, tiled-attn, and safe_attention. also try quantization variations q4f vs q5 to see memory tradeoffs.
[03:22] Samir: what about batching? we saw increased latency when we enabled large batching because it waits to fill.
[03:28] Priya: we recommend dynamic batching with latency cap — small time window (10-20ms) so we don't hurt TTFT. we also suggest workload-aware routing: route low latency routes to low-batch pods, background batch jobs to separate instance pools.
[03:44] Jordan: can Redwood do that routing automatically in Dedicated?
[03:48] Alex: yes, we have smart routing policies — cost vs latency tiers. we can demo routing rules in the console; priya can show a config snippet.
[03:57] Priya: i'll paste an example in the doc.
[04:00] Alex: quick numbers review — current baseline (from last week's canary) 95th pct end-to-end: 780ms; today's targeted run with cache+fast kernels brought baseline 95th to ~640ms for mixed-profiles; TTFT median moved from 210ms to 165ms.
[04:15] Jordan: so about a 20% tail improvement, that's encouraging. what's the expected improvement if we switch to a dedicated kernel build we discussed?
[04:22] Priya: if we enable the custom compiled kernel path (kernel tuning for rivermark), we estimate another 10-15% tail reduction for 256-sized sequences based on internal sims. we'll need one test run to validate.
[04:34] Samir: any risks with custom kernel? like determinism or accuracy regressions?
[04:38] Priya: good point — functional tests run in CI; we wouldn't ship kernels without passing accuracy/evaluation. the main risk is build stability across different CUDA driver versions, which is why we test on your vm images.
[04:50] Maya: about drivers — our infra team is on older driver 520.x. do you need a newer driver for some kernels?
[04:57] Priya: some asm kernels need >=525. if you can't upgrade we'll fall back to tiled-attn which still gives gains but slightly less. we'll capture that in the run matrix.
[05:07] Tina: on compliance, we need audit logs for rollouts and kernel updates; can you log kernel versions and rollout events?
[05:14] Alex: yes audit events for model, kernel, and rollout are captured in Redwood Console; we can forward logs to your SIEM.
[05:20] Tina: please include retention times and whether logs include payloads.
[05:24] Alex: we don't include raw payloads by default; metadata and token counts are logged. will add doc note.
[05:30] Jordan: ok circling back — what do you need from us this week to run the 256/512 focused test?
[05:34] Priya: three things: 1) representative prompt sets for 256/512 (samir), 2) access to test vpc (maya), 3) target tails we'd consider acceptable (jordan).
[05:44] Samir: i'll drop the prompt set in the benchmark sheet by Friday.
[05:47] Maya: i'll provision the VPC and share a service account this week.
[05:51] Jordan: target 95th < 600ms for 256 and <900ms for 512. we'll be flexible but that's our aim.
[06:00] Priya: noted. next i want to mention a subtle transcription note — (laugh) no, sorry, i mean a subtle perf tuning: pre-tokenization on the client reduced server CPU by about 12% in our run. if you can tokenize closer to the edge it helps TTFT.
[06:15] Jordan: we can do that for sure.
[06:17] Alex: quick demo ask — priya can you run streaming+fast-attn-asm on one pod in your test cluster and attach traces to the sheet?
[06:25] Priya: yes i'll run that and attach trace logs. expect traces and a config diff.
[06:30] Jordan: if kernel fallback still happens under load, can we do a graceful degrade to a smaller model variant?
[06:36] Priya: yes we can route to a compatible variant — Redwood supports auto-fallback to smaller quantized model. you'll see slight quality diff but huge latency wins.
[06:45] Samir: we want to see quality comparisons side-by-side; can you attach a small eval set?
[06:50] Priya: yes we'll run the eval harness and put output in the sheet.
[06:53] Maya: any infra changes needed to test kernel build? only driver concern?
[06:57] Priya: mainly drivers and the container runtime. we'll provide an image with tuned kernels; if you can't run that image in private due to policy we can run tests in Dedicated and share traces.
[07:08] Jordan: budget question — will moving to a custom kernel increase our cost for Dedicated?
[07:12] Alex: kernel itself doesn't change pricing, but if you need a larger instance class to avoid memory pressure that affects cost. we can model that in the spreadsheet.
[07:20] Tina: security follow-up — can we get SOC2 docs and the kernel build reproducibility notes?
[07:25] Alex: yes i'll include SOC2 and reproducibility notes in the follow-up.
[07:29] Priya: ok quick recap of owners: priya runs perf suite (256/512 + kernels + q4/q5) and attaches traces; alex shares benchmark sheet and kernel config; maya provisions VPC and creds; samir shares prompt sets and target criteria; tina will review security notes when shared.
[07:47] Jordan: great thanks. anything else?
[07:50] Liam: just to call out that we'll track logs and the canary schedule in the CRM deal — i'll add the milestone.
[07:56] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the spreadsheet link and test plan.
[07:59] Jordan: thanks all, bye.
